Budget-cooking blogs

People who cook dinner nightly on a real grocery budget and write down what actually worked. One photo per recipe, no diet-culture lectures, and per-serving cost where it matters. Blurb note: two lines each — what it is, why you’d flip to it tonight.

The picks

Budget Bytes

The benchmark budget blog — hundreds of tested recipes with per-serving cost, plus pantry-stocking guides that reward reading once. Tonight use: sort the index by ingredient you already own, pick the cheapest per-serving match, done. The comment sections often catch substitutions.

Frugal Feeding

A UK-based blog of genuinely frugal, from-scratch recipes where cost-cutting is the actual subject, not a tag. Tonight use: strong on stretchy mains, soups, and bread-adjacent ideas that use cheap staples instead of special anything.

Cheap Recipe Blog

Short, ingredient-cheap recipes with a knack for turning condiments and odd pantry goods into actual dinner. Tonight use: the “what to do with half a can of X” energy is exactly what a Sunday-was-yesterday fridge demands.

Good Cheap Eats

No-panic, home-cooking-on-a-budget writing with batch-cooking logic baked into nearly every recipe. Tonight use: when tonight’s dinner should also quietly feed Thursday — the structure of the recipes supports cooking once.

$5 Dinners

Long-running blog whose whole premise is in the name: feed the whole family dinner for about five dollars. Tonight use: many recipes are price-point-anchored, so shop the loss-leaders and this page supplies the plan for the rest of the week.

Cooking on a Bootstrap

Jack Monroe’s stark-raving-honest writing about hunger budgets, with recipes measured in pennies and real quantities. Tonight use: the UK staple-list recipes are a masterclass in flavor-per-penny; convert weights if needed and your own budget will notice.
